output.headline: A sponsor with prior deals in the target's own sub-sector, including one in the Midwest, and a record of paying above the comparable upper quartile.
output.differentiator: Its 17.1x median multiple paid sits above the comparable-deal upper quartile of 15.3x, and it has already bought in the target's own sub-sector, including a Midwest deal. [T:record, V:comps, D:MA-2021-0407]
output.why_them: Prior Healthcare Services deals; pays above the upper quartile

acquirer_overview.title: A large sponsor with a ten-year, mostly closed deal record
points: Financial sponsor with 25 deals from 2015 to 2024; 22 of 25 (88%) closed and 23 of 25 (92%) were control deals. [T:record, K:closed_share, K:control_share]
Private Equity segment manages $416.4 billion of Total Assets Under Management as of December 31, 2025. [P:1]
Home sub-sector is Health Insurance (6 deals), so the target is a step into services rather than its core. [B:buyer, K:by_sub_sector]

strategic_fit_thesis.title: Services precedents give a credible, if not core, fit
points: Two deals in the target's own sub-sector and 7 in adjacent provider sub-sectors; sector relevance is a modest factor for it. [T:record, S:sector_rel]
Platform Build is a stated motive in 9 of 25 deals, against 23% of all deals in the file. [M:platform_build]
No open platform in the sub-sector, so the target would be a new position rather than an add-on. Size fit is its one sponsor angle. [A:angles]

precedent_activity.title: Relevant precedents are recent, mid-sized and priced at 10.0x to 14.6x
points: Peak Medical Management: $342M SPAC Merger, 2021, Midwest, Healthcare Services, 10.0x EBITDA. [D:MA-2021-0407]
Evergreen Care Solutions: $299M Bolt-on Acquisition, 2021, Healthcare Services, 14.6x EBITDA. [D:MA-2021-0195]
Dental deals: Crest Oral Health, $558M LBO, 13.5x; North Smile Group, $222M Management Buyout, 13.5x; both 2021. [D:MA-2021-0164, D:MA-2021-0453]

valuation_context.title: Upper-quartile pricing is defensible, but returns at the ask are thin
points: Comparable range across 70 deals: 10.7x at the 25th percentile, 12.8x median and 15.3x at the 75th. [V:comps]
The 75th percentile is defensible: the target's 16.8% margin sits above the comps' median of 12.9%. Blackstone's own median paid is 17.1x. [V:comps]
With 5.0x leverage at 8.5%, the equity cheque is $128M and IRR at the ask is 18.7% against a 20% target. [V:lbo]

risk_flags.title: Return at the asking price
risk_flags.concern: IRR at the ask of 18.7% is below its 20% target. [V:lbo]
risk_flags.mitigant: A platform exit at 15.0x lifts the maximum price to $216M. [V:lbo]
risk_flags.reality: Maximum price at the same exit is $193M, so the bid depends on underwriting the platform exit. [V:lbo]

risk_flags.title: Thin regional and platform fit
risk_flags.concern: Prior purchases in this or a neighbouring region are a slight factor against, and there is no open platform. [S:geo_fit, A:angles]
risk_flags.mitigant: Peak Medical Management was a Midwest deal in the target's own sub-sector. [D:MA-2021-0407]
risk_flags.reality: Only 2 of its 25 deals were in the Midwest. [T:record]

risk_flags.title: Core focus elsewhere
risk_flags.concern: 16 of its 25 deals were outside provider services, and its home sub-sector is Health Insurance. [T:record, B:buyer]
risk_flags.mitigant: It has 2 own-sub-sector deals and 7 in adjacent provider sub-sectors. [T:record]
risk_flags.reality: Provider deals are 9 of 25, a real but secondary part of its record. [A:angles]

conviction.rationale: Supported by 2 deals in the target's own sub-sector and 7 in adjacent provider sub-sectors; held back because there is no open platform in the sub-sector. [C:conviction]
